text:
I wish someone told me this earlier:

People won't always understand your choices, and they don't have to.

The ones who understand, will.
The ones who don't, won't.

Because they're seeing your life through their own fears, limits, and priorities.

You're the only one living with the consequences of your decisions.
Trust your gut.

Life becomes much easier when you stop explaining; start doing.

Quote from Beyond the Syllabus.: PEOPLE WON'T ALWAYS UNDERSTAND YOUR CHOICES.
MAKE THEM ANYWAY.
As long as it feels right to you, THAT'S ENOUGH.

Growth isn’t about rushing to the finish line.
It’s about building the parts of you that no one can take away:

- Your body and health - to support you in the long-run.
- Your skills - sharpened through practice and persistence.
- Your mindset - trained to look for possibility, not limitation.
- Your character - defined by your values, not circumstances.
- Your knowledge - expanded through curiosity and learning.
- Your work ethic - steady and consistent, even when motivation fades.

These are the foundations that make you unstoppable.

And every time you choose to reset and keep going, you’re proving that the most important project in your life (you) is worth the work.

No one, and I mean absolutely no one, is happier about their child's success than a parent.

Quite often, that success has got nothing to do with external achievements.
More to do with how happy you are in your life.

Your parents want exactly the same things for you that you want for yourself.

The path may be different.
But the destination is the same.

Quote: Pray for just one thing: That your parents live long enough to witness your success.

Being laid off is never just about losing a job.

It’s about losing a piece of your identity.
The routine, the purpose, the pride.

Here is something I wish I could tell all of them:

If you go on to live for 80 years, then this moment will mean nothing!

I know it hurts at the moment.

You are suddenly nothing for the company that you gave everything to.
I understand it might make you angry.

For many days, it will be the first thing you will think of, every morning.

Until one day it won’t be.

Use this time to rediscover yourself.
To build what you always wanted.
To prove to yourself what you’re made of.

Give yourself some time, my friend.

Everything will be alright.
As it always has been.

PS: I share more insights to help you build the right mindset.
Follow me to stay updated.

Quote via Justin Welsh: You were freed

If the climb is tough, but needs to be done,
Ignore the mountain in front of you.

Take the smallest possible step forward to get you started.
Keep doing that every single day.

The pro is the amateur who showed up every day

“What are your salary expectations?”

One of the most confounding questions in an interview.

Many say, “Whatever fits your budget.”
But the right way to answer is:

“Based on my research and this role’s responsibilities, professionals with my experience earn between X and Y.

How does that fit into your budget?”

Notice that you’re not asking for this salary.

You’re stating what the market pays.
It shows you’ve done your homework and you’re confident in your value.

Try this next time.
You’ll be surprised how the conversation shifts.

Everyone wants to be an expert.
Few are willing to be a beginner.

I was stuck at 7,000 subscribers on YouTube for 4 years.
I could’ve easily given up.

But if I did, I wouldn’t have reached 2 million subscribers in the next 2 years.
Which is 6+ million today.

Failure isn’t embarrassment.
Every ‘expert’ once looked unsure, awkward, or even ridiculous.

It’s proof that you’re in motion, learning, growing.

If you're in that phase, don’t be ashamed.
It means you’re doing the brave work most avoid.

I’m rooting for you :))

Their Day 15 looks effortless.
But you didn’t see the 14 messy days before it.

So don’t compare your Day 1 to someone else’s Day 15.
The only fair comparison is with who you were yesterday.

If you're moving forward, even slowly, you’re growing.

Give yourself permission to take the messy route.
The courage to stay on your own path.

Because that’s how you reach your Day 15.

You’ve got this! Quote: Don’t compare your Day 1 to someone else’s Day 15.

Knowing when to say no (and saying it) is a life skill.

Even though it may seem difficult, say no when something doesn’t serve your best interests.

When you have to go against your values.
When you have to be someone you are not.

Because every time you say no to what’s wrong for you,
You’re saying yes to what’s right for you.

There’s nothing selfish about that.

It’s self-respect.

And if you don’t put yourself first, who will?, Quote: Every time you say no to what’s wrong for you, you’re saying yes to what’s right for you.

"Start seeing failure this way and you stop fearing it:

Failure is feedback.
Failure is redirection.
Failure tells you where you can do better next time.

Over time, every failure passes away.

ONLY if you reflect on it.
ONLY if you ask yourself: Why did it happen?
ONLY if you change the way you do things.

Because we will all fail.
But few of us will win in life.
That will happen through reflection.

The more you fail and adapt, the closer you get to success."

"They tell you, “You’ve changed.”
But that doesn’t mean you’re wrong.

It means you’re on different points of your journeys, as growth often is.

Not all friendships are meant to last.

Appreciate the past, but walk alongside those whose journeys align with yours."

"We seek validation.
We want someone to tell us we're on the right path.

But here's the truth:

The more proof you give yourself that you're growing, the less permission you'll need from others to keep going.

When you look back at your week and realise:

"I handled that conversation better,"
"I showed up when I didn't feel like it,"
"I stayed patient when I usually don't,"

That's growth.

And a sense of growth is the most honest form of self-validation."

"The internet is the only place where you can go from $40k to $400k in one year.

- No career path
- No activity bonus
- No daily meetings
- No 'can I have a raise?'
- No performance reviews
- No, 'we don't have the budget'

It all starts with the concept of learning how to accumulate attention.

Once you get attention, you can use that as leverage and point it any direction you please.

So, start by learning to get some attention here on LinkedIn."

"Your time is money.

Don’t sell it by:

- Reading trash
- Arguing online
- Endlessly scrolling

Invest it in:

- Learning a skill
- Writing content about it
- Building a product people can buy

Only you know your true hourly rate."

"Most people quit right before it would have worked.

They start strong.
Overthink by month 2.
Give up by month 6.

Then call it bad luck.

The only difference between those who make it and those who don't?

They stayed in the game longer.

That's it.

No secret strategy.
No perfect timing.
No special talent.

Just:

• Pick one thing you're good at
• Do it in public here on LinkedIn
• Get 1% better each week
• Don't stop

Here's what my timeline looked like:

Month 1: Talking to myself
Month 6: First real response
Month 12: Consistent engagement
Month 18: More opportunities than time

Everyone who's built something real has a similar story.

We all started with crickets.
We all wanted to quit.
We all felt foolish.

The difference? We kept showing up anyway.

Stop waiting for the perfect moment.
Start stacking small wins instead."

"It’s harder for older people to remain creative as they lose the ability to look at things from a brand new perspective.

Most innovation comes from young people or young companies run by young people."
"Degrees are often a proof of someone being good at diagnosing a problem versus solving them."

"People buy hope from everywhere, efficiency from very limited places.

As most hope is bought in hope."

Humans are subconsciously always stuck in ranking and comparing mode and when someone hits a misfortune our primitive brain gives us a dopamine rush as if we got a mega boost in our own rank.

Schadenfreude is easy to understand if we treat world as one big zero sum game.
Empowerment without accountability ends up as entitlement.

Leadership is about uncomfortable conversations and decisions.

Great leadership is doing both without delay.

Large language models grow by relentlessly ingesting diverse data. True for our mind too. It’s best to keep sampling new disciplines and trends to keep evolving our mental algorithms.

When success makes curiosity shrink, our personal ‘LLM’ stops learning and starts coasting.
It’s hard to be wealthy if you’re not surrounded by people who value their time a lot.

Envy of someone’s genetic or inherited gifts is futile as it’s just luck. Envy of someone’s earned success is misdirected as it’s a signal of lessons you’ve yet to learn.

Envy reveals what you desire, but not the path to get there.

Be around people who happen to universe.

Life is too short to be around those who are net takers from the universe.
Introverts who hate managing people may be first to automate most things with AI.
AI made me realize a clear sign of intelligence is someone’s ability to quickly grasp something complex without providing a ton of context.
AI may force freshers to become entrepreneurs due to lack of entry level jobs.
If a knowledgeable person doesn’t use their knowledge to build, they may end up using their knowledge to judge and become a cynic.
